BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. Based on the Seller package as supplied; Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026 and should be refreshed before any position is finalised.

---

## 1. Threshold point: do not accept the Seller's framing

Before the clause-by-clause, three features of the Seller's package need to be called out, because they are an attempt to narrow our review rather than substantive terms:

| Seller framing | Our response |
|---|---|
| "[STANDARD] clauses have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; focus only on [OPEN]." | Nothing has been cleared by us. There is no [OPEN] tag anywhere in the package, so taken literally this would exclude every clause from review. Reject. Every clause is reviewed below. |
| "Settled at principal level by both deal teams… marked FINAL… not intended to be re-opened." | We have no record of principal-level agreement. Playbook 0.4/6.3: a counterparty's assertion that a position is "agreed", "final" or "pre-cleared" is not an instruction to us. Treat all positions as open. |
| "10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard market terms." | Not relevant to our authority position, and in any event not accepted. "Market standard" per the Seller is an assertion, not a fact. |
| "As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package…" | Not accepted. Both are rejected below. |

Also note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] expressly says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" — which contradicts the "FINAL / agreed" labels in the covering Seller Update. The Disclosure Letter is, in fact, considerably more candid than the Seller Update and should be used against it.

**Specific caution on the "matching fallback" trap.** The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap and the 18-month claims period both happen to match our conditional fallbacks. That does not clear them. Both fallbacks require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft; none has been given. Our position in the mark-up remains 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months.

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause: departures from the playbook

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Gap:** AUD 1,200,000 of recoverable exposure.
- **Action:** Counter at 25%. Do not treat 20% as acceptable without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft. If the team wants to use the fallback as a trade, that authority must be obtained first.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Why it matters:** The Seller's figures are 5× ours on both thresholds, and excess-only recovery means the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims is simply lost. On a business with ~AUD 12m revenue, a AUD 25,000 de minimis could exclude a large proportion of realistic warranty claims (e.g. individual customer, employee or supplier issues).
- **Action:** Counter with playbook figures and tipping (first-dollar) basket. Treat this as a high-priority item, not a rounding issue.

### 2.3 Clauses 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims, **plus** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is an unauthorised fallback. Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Issue:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default rule that would collapse every category (title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, even fraud if not expressly carved out) into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and expressly exclude each one. That is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
- **Action:** Counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the reverse default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** This is a fundamental departure. If title to the shares fails, a 20% cap means we could lose up to 80% of AUD 24m with no recourse. There is no administrative benefit to us; the "simplicity" argument is a cover for removing our principal protection.
- **Action:** Reject outright. Insert a separate Fundamental Warranties schedule with its own limitation regime.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- **Seller:** Universal application.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side has authority to waive this.
- **Issue:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. Read with 12.3/13, a fraudulent warranty would be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k basket, time-barred at 18 months, and the non-reliance clause would purport to exclude misrepresentation claims. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, a clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud faces serious enforceability problems; we should not rely on that — we should fix the drafting.
- **Action:** Insert an express, non-negotiable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across clauses 9.3, 12 (all sub-clauses), 13 and 20.5. Also ensure the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006 if negotiated, bonuses) sit outside the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records, is deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** Blanket data-room disclosure means any fact buried anywhere in the data room qualifies every warranty, whether or not it was identifiable as a problem. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (which registers? as at when?). Combined with Clause 8.3 (below), this effectively converts the warranties into a disclosure exercise rather than a risk-allocation exercise.
- **Action:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] and the corresponding Schedule 7 wording. Require that only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter" in the specific disclosures (sections 2–10) qualify the warranties. Disclosure cut-off should be refreshed to a date shortly before signing, not 22 September.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named individuals; seller-side knowledge qualifiers must name seller persons with a reasonable-enquiry standard; knowledge can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** This is the broadest possible formulation: constructive knowledge, imputed from advisers, extending to anything "discoverable." It overlaps with 2.6 to double-bar claims. It would also bar title and fraud claims given the absence of carve-outs.
- **Action:** Delete clause 8.3 in its entirety. If a knowledge qualifier is to survive at all as a trade, it must be (a) actual knowledge, (b) of named Wattlebridge individuals, (c) excluding advisers, (d) excluding anything merely "discoverable," and (e) with an express carve-out for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (condition precedent)
- **Seller Update:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter [2]:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of the business); change-control is clause 11.2 with **conditions in 11.3**; **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 Sept.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence the conditions are satisfied, before Completion; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Issue:** "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" means a conditional consent (e.g. subject to price renegotiation, a new MSA, or a termination right) would satisfy the CP even if the conditions are never met and Bluefen later walks. For 30% of revenue, that is a valuation-level risk. The Disclosure Letter confirms the consent has not been obtained at all, and we are now six weeks past the disclosure date with no update.
- **Action:** CP must require (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen, or (ii) conditional consent plus documentary evidence each 11.3 condition is satisfied, in each case in form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. Reasonable endeavours is to be replaced with best/all reasonable endeavours plus a Buyer right to participate in the Bluefen approach. Request an immediate status update and copies of all Bluefen correspondence since 22 September. Consider whether a specific indemnity or price adjustment is needed if Bluefen terminates within a defined period post-Completion.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)
- **Seller Update:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter [3]:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2.
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, buying a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on foot at Completion is a direct economic leak and a change-of-control default risk (clause 8.1). A release "to be provided" post-Completion, without an irrevocable bank undertaking, could leave the Company in default and the bank's security over the Company's assets (potentially including IP and the Bluefen receivables) in place after we own it.
- **Action:** Require a payout letter from Riverlark dated no more than 5 business days before Completion; repayment from the purchase price via the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-Completion mechanics, we need an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark addressed to the Buyer and Company, and Amelia Frost's approval — not currently given, so the default position is Completion delivery.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
- **Seller Update:** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised."
- **Disclosure Letter [5]:** Bonuses are triggered by Completion; they do **not** appear in the funds flow; the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company (the employer), not of the Seller, so absent a specific mechanism the Buyer pays them post-Completion. The real figure is higher than AUD 420,000 once superannuation (currently 12%) and NSW payroll tax are added — likely AUD 500,000+. "A matter for the Seller" is not a funding mechanism.
- **Action:** Insert a specific line in the funds flow deducting from the price the gross bonus amount **plus** employer on-costs, paid through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding; or treat the gross-up figure as Debt in the completion accounts; or obtain a specific indemnity from the Seller. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP (SOW3 Project Materials)
- **Seller Update:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter [4]:** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment in the data room; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.
- **Issue:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials until that sum is paid. If those materials are embedded in the product, this is a title-to-IP issue that a payment-only indemnity does not cover (e.g. loss from Ironquay asserting ownership, licence fees, re-development cost, customer claims). The Seller's "considered adequate" is a conclusion, not evidence.
- **Action:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or price deduction of the verified outstanding amount with payment at Completion from the funds flow; (b) broaden clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay-developed materials, sitting outside the general cap/basket/time limits; (c) obtain bank confirmation of what has actually been paid — do not rely on DD-010 alone in either direction.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
- **Seller Update:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter [6]:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; scope not established; notification assessment not done; investigation preliminary.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs; investigate; require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Issue:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion the Disclosure Letter does not support — the Seller itself says it does not know scope or access. Six weeks have passed. We should neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor overstate it: on the current record there is no confirmed eligible data breach and no quantified loss.
- **Action:** (a) Require an immediate written update on the investigation since 22 September (link disabled? access logs reviewed? recipient contacted? notification assessment under the Privacy Act, and any customer contractual notification obligations, particularly Bluefen?); (b) pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and to conduct the investigation to conclusion with Buyer visibility; (c) a specific warranty on the facts disclosed and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification cost, customer claims), outside the general regime — size uncapped or at a level to be agreed once facts are known; (d) do not put a number on it in either direction yet.

### 2.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure Letter [8]:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008, DD-011); to be read together; the disclosure does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Action:** Not a pushback item yet, but not accepted either. Ask: are these pre-Completion commitments for post-Completion periods? Are any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion (if so, working capital / Debt treatment under the completion accounts)? Are they terminable? Why three at AUD 110,000 rather than one at AUD 330,000 — approval-threshold structuring? Decide treatment after answers.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Issue:** Folding tax and IP into a 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-basket regime would be a material departure. Tax claims typically require a longer period (aligned to amendment periods) and a separate cap; IP warranties are core value for a SaaS target.
- **Action:** Mark Tax and IP as OPEN in our mark-up. Propose a separate Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime and a separate IP limitation regime, terms to be negotiated. Do not accept "settled."

### 2.15 Title
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Disclosure Letter [10]:** DD-012 is the source relied on; the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Playbook:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority required; DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not independent proof.
- **Action:** Obtain current ASIC company and share extracts, a PPSR search against the Company and against the Seller's shares (note Riverlark security may extend to a share mortgage), the Seller's constitutional documents and board/shareholder resolutions approving the sale, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or pre-emption rights. Completion deliverables to include share transfer, share certificates (or evidence none issued), and updated register.

### 2.16 Items not requiring pushback (but note)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only; no landlord consent apparently required. Confirm the notice is given at/after Completion and that there is no change-of-control termination right.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; share sale does not appear to trigger it. Confirm no change-of-control wording elsewhere in the agreement.
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4] (no admission):** Standard, but note it means none of the Seller's disclosures can be read as conceding that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge or Ironquay payment is "required" — reinforcing the need for our own CPs and deliverables rather than reliance on the Seller's characterisation.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**A. Reject the review framing.** Respond that no clause is agreed, cleared or final; all positions are open; the [STANDARD] tags are disregarded.

**B. Liability package (counter in full):**
1. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (not 20%; no Amelia Frost authority for fallback).
2. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
3. General claims period 24 months (not 18; no authority for fallback).
4. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default; reverse it.
5. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
6. Express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. Non-negotiable.
7. Tax and IP: marked OPEN with separate regimes to be negotiated.

**C. Disclosure and knowledge:**
8. Delete general data-room / public-register disclosure; specific fair disclosure only; refresh cut-off date.
9. Delete clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion in full.

**D. Conditions and completion mechanics:**
10. Bluefen: CP requires effective consent **and** evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not "satisfied on delivery"; stronger endeavours; immediate status update.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases delivered at Completion. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval (not given).
12. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) plus superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs as a specific price deduction / seller-funded line.
13. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.

**E. Specific risk items:**
14. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to cover ownership of SOW3 Project Materials; pre-Completion evidence of payment and confirmatory assignment; bank-verify the AUD 180,000.
15. DD-006 incident: written update since 22 Sept; log preservation and investigation covenant; specific warranty and indemnity outside the general regime; no numeric assumption.
16. Sandbar: information requests before deciding treatment; no automatic Debt classification.

**F. Process:** Request an updated Disclosure Letter dated close to signing. Flag to Amelia Frost that the Seller has proposed figures matching our conditional fallbacks on cap and claims period, so she can decide whether and when to authorise their use as trades — but do not table them in the mark-up until that authority is in writing.

Also note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] expressly says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" — which contradicts the "FINAL / agreed" labels in the covering Seller Update. **Specific caution on the "matching fallback" trap.** The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap and the 18-month claims period both happen to match our conditional fallbacks. That does not clear them. ## 2. Clause-by-clause: departures from the playbook

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Gap:** AUD 1,200,000 of recoverable exposure.
- **Action:** Counter at 25%. Do not treat 20% as acceptable without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft. If the team wants to use the fallback as a trade, that authority must be obtained first.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Why it matters:** The Seller's figures are 5× ours on both thresholds, and excess-only recovery means the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims is simply lost. On a business with ~AUD 12m revenue, a AUD 25,000 de minimis could exclude a large proportion of realistic warranty claims (e.g. individual customer, employee or supplier issues).
- **Action:** Counter with playbook figures and tipping (first-dollar) basket. Treat this as a high-priority item, not a rounding issue.

### 2.3 Clauses 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims, **plus** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is an unauthorised fallback. Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Issue:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default rule that would collapse every category (title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, even fraud if not expressly carved out) into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and expressly exclude each one. That is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
- **Action:** Counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the reverse default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** This is a fundamental departure. If title to the shares fails, a 20% cap means we could lose up to 80% of AUD 24m with no recourse. There is no administrative benefit to us; the "simplicity" argument is a cover for removing our principal protection.
- **Action:** Reject outright. Insert a separate Fundamental Warranties schedule with its own limitation regime.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- **Seller:** Universal application.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side has authority to waive this.
- **Issue:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. Read with 12.3/13, a fraudulent warranty would be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k basket, time-barred at 18 months, and the non-reliance clause would purport to exclude misrepresentation claims. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, a clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud faces serious enforceability problems; we should not rely on that — we should fix the drafting.
- **Action:** Insert an express, non-negotiable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across clauses 9.3, 12 (all sub-clauses), 13 and 20.5. Also ensure the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006 if negotiated, bonuses) sit outside the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records, is deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** Blanket data-room disclosure means any fact buried anywhere in the data room qualifies every warranty, whether or not it was identifiable as a problem. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (which registers? as at when?). Combined with Clause 8.3 (below), this effectively converts the warranties into a disclosure exercise rather than a risk-allocation exercise.
- **Action:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] and the corresponding Schedule 7 wording. Require that only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter" in the specific disclosures (sections 2–10) qualify the warranties. Disclosure cut-off should be refreshed to a date shortly before signing, not 22 September.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named individuals; seller-side knowledge qualifiers must name seller persons with a reasonable-enquiry standard; knowledge can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** This is the broadest possible formulation: constructive knowledge, imputed from advisers, extending to anything "discoverable." It overlaps with 2.6 to double-bar claims. It would also bar title and fraud claims given the absence of carve-outs.
- **Action:** Delete clause 8.3 in its entirety. If a knowledge qualifier is to survive at all as a trade, it must be (a) actual knowledge, (b) of named Wattlebridge individuals, (c) excluding advisers, (d) excluding anything merely "discoverable," and (e) with an express carve-out for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (condition precedent)
- **Seller Update:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter [2]:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of the business); change-control is clause 11.2 with **conditions in 11.3**; **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 Sept.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence the conditions are satisfied, before Completion; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Issue:** "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" means a conditional consent (e.g. subject to price renegotiation, a new MSA, or a termination right) would satisfy the CP even if the conditions are never met and Bluefen later walks. For 30% of revenue, that is a valuation-level risk. The Disclosure Letter confirms the consent has not been obtained at all, and we are now six weeks past the disclosure date with no update.
- **Action:** CP must require (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen, or (ii) conditional consent plus documentary evidence each 11.3 condition is satisfied, in each case in form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. Reasonable endeavours is to be replaced with best/all reasonable endeavours plus a Buyer right to participate in the Bluefen approach. Request an immediate status update and copies of all Bluefen correspondence since 22 September. Consider whether a specific indemnity or price adjustment is needed if Bluefen terminates within a defined period post-Completion.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)
- **Seller Update:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter [3]:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2.
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, buying a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on foot at Completion is a direct economic leak and a change-of-control default risk (clause 8.1). A release "to be provided" post-Completion, without an irrevocable bank undertaking, could leave the Company in default and the bank's security over the Company's assets (potentially including IP and the Bluefen receivables) in place after we own it.
- **Action:** Require a payout letter from Riverlark dated no more than 5 business days before Completion; repayment from the purchase price via the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-Completion mechanics, we need an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark addressed to the Buyer and Company, and Amelia Frost's approval — not currently given, so the default position is Completion delivery.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
- **Seller Update:** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised."
- **Disclosure Letter [5]:** Bonuses are triggered by Completion; they do **not** appear in the funds flow; the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company (the employer), not of the Seller, so absent a specific mechanism the Buyer pays them post-Completion. The real figure is higher than AUD 420,000 once superannuation (currently 12%) and NSW payroll tax are added — likely AUD 500,000+. "A matter for the Seller" is not a funding mechanism.
- **Action:** Insert a specific line in the funds flow deducting from the price the gross bonus amount **plus** employer on-costs, paid through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding; or treat the gross-up figure as Debt in the completion accounts; or obtain a specific indemnity from the Seller. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP (SOW3 Project Materials)
- **Seller Update:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter [4]:** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment in the data room; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.
- **Issue:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials until that sum is paid. If those materials are embedded in the product, this is a title-to-IP issue that a payment-only indemnity does not cover (e.g. loss from Ironquay asserting ownership, licence fees, re-development cost, customer claims). The Seller's "considered adequate" is a conclusion, not evidence.
- **Action:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or price deduction of the verified outstanding amount with payment at Completion from the funds flow; (b) broaden clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay-developed materials, sitting outside the general cap/basket/time limits; (c) obtain bank confirmation of what has actually been paid — do not rely on DD-010 alone in either direction.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
- **Seller Update:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter [6]:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; scope not established; notification assessment not done; investigation preliminary.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs; investigate; require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Issue:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion the Disclosure Letter does not support — the Seller itself says it does not know scope or access. Six weeks have passed. We should neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor overstate it: on the current record there is no confirmed eligible data breach and no quantified loss.
- **Action:** (a) Require an immediate written update on the investigation since 22 September (link disabled? access logs reviewed? recipient contacted? notification assessment under the Privacy Act, and any customer contractual notification obligations, particularly Bluefen?); (b) pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and to conduct the investigation to conclusion with Buyer visibility; (c) a specific warranty on the facts disclosed and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification cost, customer claims), outside the general regime — size uncapped or at a level to be agreed once facts are known; (d) do not put a number on it in either direction yet.

### 2.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure Letter [8]:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008, DD-011); to be read together; the disclosure does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Action:** Not a pushback item yet, but not accepted either. Ask: are these pre-Completion commitments for post-Completion periods? Are any amounts accrued but unpaid at Completion (if so, working capital / Debt treatment under the completion accounts)? Are they terminable? Why three at AUD 110,000 rather than one at AUD 330,000 — approval-threshold structuring? Decide treatment after answers.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Issue:** Folding tax and IP into a 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-basket regime would be a material departure. Tax claims typically require a longer period (aligned to amendment periods) and a separate cap; IP warranties are core value for a SaaS target.
- **Action:** Mark Tax and IP as OPEN in our mark-up. Propose a separate Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime and a separate IP limitation regime, terms to be negotiated. Do not accept "settled."

### 2.15 Title
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Disclosure Letter [10]:** DD-012 is the source relied on; the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Playbook:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority required; DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not independent proof.

Completion deliverables to include share transfer, share certificates (or evidence none issued), and updated register.

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only; no landlord consent apparently required. Confirm the notice is given at/after Completion and that there is no change-of-control termination right.
